data.raw_text:
John Basilone was born November 4th, 1916 in Buffalo, NY.
-
Two years later his family would move back to Raritan, NJ where he would grow up. He enlisted in the US Army in 1934 and would serve with the 16th Infantry and then the 31st Infantry serving a tour in the Philippines where he made quite a name for himself, “Manila John,” as champion boxer.
-
Once his contract ended he drove truck for his brother-in-law in MD before enlisting in the Marine Corps in 1940.
-
He would go on to be awarded the Medal of Honor for actions on Guadalcanal when his sections of D Co 1/7 Heavy Guns, attached to C Co, were attacked by members of the Japanese Sendai Division on Lunga Ridge, IVO Henderson Field. (See my posts from October 24/25.)
-
He was then sent on a war bond drive back in the states. Soon, he had enough of that and wanted to get back with the boys.
-
After his request to return to the fleet was approved, Basilone was assigned to C Co 1/27. On February 19, 1945, the first day of the invasion of Iwo Jima, he was serving as a machine gun section leader on Red Beach II. While the Marines landed, the Japanese concentrated their fire at the incoming Marines from heavily fortified blockhouses staged throughout the island. With his unit pinned down, Basilone made his way around the side of the Japanese positions until he was directly on top of the blockhouse. He then attacked with grenades and demolitions, single-handedly destroying the entire strong point and its defending garrison. He then made his way toward Airfield Number 1 where he would be killed in action but not before helping guide a Sherman through a minefield. For his actions on Iwo, he would be posthumously awarded the Navy Cross. 
-
If you get to Arlington, pay him a visit. Grave 384 Section 12.
-
Rest Easy Gunny. The guns are still up!
-
The first photo was colorized for @john_basilone_parade_committee

INC RALLY FROM NOV. 16-18

A source confirmed to The STAR that executive director Cecille Lorenzana-Romero of the National Parks Development Committee, which manages Rizal Park, approved the INC's request last Thursday.

Cesar Chavez, chief of staff of Manila Mayor Isko Moreno, said they would provide "perimeter support" for the INC rally.

"While we know that the INC is very organized whenever it holds a rally, the city government of Manila would be deploying teams to monitor and to provide assistance outside the Rizal Park," Chavez said.

The Manila Police District would also be providing security outside the perimeter area and traffic enforcers would man the flow of vehicles during the three-day event. | via @EZMacairan
